newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows 40 pct foreign stakes in airlines.
newsitem.headline: India allows 40 pct foreign stakes in airlines.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday approved a domestic aviation policy allowing foreign investors to take equity stakes of up to 40 percent in domestic airlines, but analysts said it fell short of expectations.

"The decision is to go along with the existing policy which permits 40 percent equity in domestic airlines," Yogesh Chandra, the highest ranking civil servant in Civil Aviation Ministry, told a news conference.

The government has allowed foreign stakes on a case-by-case basis since India allowed private airlines under a economic reform programme launched in 1991. The policy announced on Friday sets out a general rule on foreign stakes.
But the cabinet deferred a crucial decision whether to allow foreign airlines or airport companies to participate directly in the equity holding of domestic counterparts.
"This move does not imply any involvement of foreign airlines in domestic aviation tie-ups," Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim told Reuters.
"It effectively means that foreign individuals can create a company and hold a 40 percent stake," he said.
Chandra said the issue of allowing foreign airlines and airports to participate in equity holding in an Indian venture has been referred back to the civil aviation ministry.
Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) and India's Tata group have proposed a $600 million tie-up which Ibrahim has vehemently opposed.
"Today's decision means that the proposal of a Tata-SIA tie-up is as good as dead," a senior Civil Aviation ministry official, who asked not to be identified, said.
Analysts said that the government spoke with different voices and was sending confusing signals to foreign investors.
"If they are serious about sending the right signals they have to clear this (Tata-SIA) venture," said V.V. Sivakumar, head of research at securities firm Peregrine Capital India.
On Friday, the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment also agreed that any airline controlled by an Indian national would be able to operate freely in India.
"Under the new policy any airline owned and substantially controlled by an Indian national will have the right of free entry and exit in the Indian skies," said Chandra.
The private airlines will now be able to choose freely the type and size of aircraft to fly without obtaining government permission, officials said.
The private operators can also import any type or size of aircraft provided they obtain all the necessary safety clearances from the Director-General of Civil Aviation, they said.
The cabinet also decided to raise the minimum equity base of private airlines operating smaller aircraft to 50 million rupees ($1.4 million) from 30 million.
"For larger aircraft the equity size has been increased from 100 million rupees to 300 million," Chandra said. ($1 = 36 rupees)
